appliesTo: Every hook event. Each event's own contract file lists what it adds on top of these.

inputs.name: event
inputs.description: The name of the event, such as PreTool. Useful when one workflow handles more than one hook event.

inputs.name: timestamp
inputs.description: When the agent raised the event.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.description: Context about the conversation, user, channel and agent. An object; see metadataFields.

metadataFields.name: conversationId
metadataFields.description: Unique ID of the current session.

metadataFields.name: userId
metadataFields.description: ID of the user in the channel they're chatting on, such as their Microsoft Teams user ID. Use userAadObjectId to identify a signed-in user.

metadataFields.name: userAadObjectId
metadataFields.description: Microsoft Entra object ID of the signed-in user.

metadataFields.name: userDisplayName
metadataFields.description: Display name of the signed-in user.

metadataFields.name: channel
metadataFields.description: The channel the conversation is on, such as msteams.

metadataFields.name: agentId
metadataFields.description: Unique ID of the agent that raised the hook.

metadataFields.name: agentName
metadataFields.description: Display name of the agent that raised the hook.

metadataFields.name: agentSchemaName
metadataFields.description: Schema name of the agent that raised the hook.

notes: Any metadata field can be empty. The user fields are empty when the person chatting isn't signed in.
All outputs on every event are optional. An empty output means the agent continues with its default behavior.
Keep the starter workflow's input and output field names. Copilot Studio uses them to decide whether a workflow fits the event.
